text:
Maya R: Heads up — CI perf on euw2 A10 pools is spiking after merge 4219, p99 token latency jumped ~2.5x. Noticed KV cache probe rates shot up around the same time.
Devon: ack, saw alerts too. Is this noisy-neighbor or a kernel selection regression?
Maya R: initial profiler suggests kernel-switch churn during short sequences. stack from profiler: 
```
kernel_selector: choose_kernel() called 12k/s -> oscillation between l4-small and l4-medium
kv_prefetch: probe_rate=8600/s (baseline ~900/s)
batching: window_shrink_count=420 -> tiny batches, higher per-token overhead
```
Samir K: That probe_rate looks wild. Any network counters? Could be probe floods from a bad prefetch loop + backpressure causing packet bursts.
Maya R: grabbed tcpstats from a pod in euw2-a10-03: 
```
RX dropped: 0
TX queue full events: 4235 in 10m
socket tx retries spike coincident with p99 spike
```
Ops Oncall: Ops saw increased NIC transmit queue time on that host group, flagged by e2e telemetry. Could be batching shrink -> more small writes -> NIC queueing.
Devon: If kernel selector flips modes on short seqs, it can cause different kernel footprints (mem/copy patterns) which change NIC bursts. Any recent changes touching kernel heuristics in merge 4219?
Maya R: Merge 4219 touched batching hysteresis thresholds + a small kv prefetch optimizer (attempt to be aggressive on cold starts). I suspect combined leads to tight loop of prefetch->evict->prefetch.
Samir K: Can we repro locally by tweaking prefetch_rate env and running loadgen with L4-A10 profile? I'll spin a run.
CI Bot: perf/latency-tests (euw2-a10) failed: p99_token_latency increased 250% — job 8821. See: https://ci.internal/8821
Maya R: Bisect note: reverting only the prefetch patch (PR 4219@file:kv_prefetch.cc change) locally reduces probe_rate to ~920/s and p99 returns near baseline. Reverting batching hysteresis change without prefetch fix doesn't help.
Devon: Good find — sounds like prefetch patch had a runaway on certain request mixes. Need to check edge-case where KV cache miss triggers multi-probe per request for small sequences.
Samir K: I ran a targeted load on euw2-like perf infra with --seq-len-dist skewed to short tails; reproduced: prefetch loop calls increased linearly with QPS. Attached profiler snippet: 
```
# top functions
kv_prefetch::maybe_prefetch  42% CPU
kv_cache::evict_handler    18%
kernel_selector::recompute 10% (calls spike when prefetch warms)
```
Maya R: Proposing immediate rollback of the prefetch optimizer in prod (can keep batching hysteresis revert for follow-up if needed). Any objections?
Devon: +1 for rollback. Also add a unit test that simulates short-seq traffic and ensures prefetch rate capped.
Ops Oncall: I can schedule the rollback now for euw2 A10 pools, target in 10m. Will monitor NIC queue and p99 after.
runtime-bot: deploy rollback pr-4227 initiated to euw2-a10 (canary 3 pods). Track: https://deploys/internal/4227
Maya R: Thanks — after canary, please run the perf smoke (`tools/perf_smoke --profile=l4-a10 --shortseq`) and paste results.
Ops Oncall: canary pass on 3 pods. perf_smoke results: baseline p99 98ms -> canary 102ms, previous bad run was 248ms. NIC queue tail latency back to normal.
Devon: OK let's ship rollback fully. Follow-ups: 1) add prefetch cap, 2) add regression test in perf CI (short-seq mix), 3) audit kernel selector exposure points so prefetch can't cause churn.
Samir K: I'll open a PR with the prefetch cap and perf test. Assigning reviewers: @Devon and @Maya.
Maya R: appreciate the quick triage. Leaving notes for postmortem: root cause = aggressive prefetch optimization interacting with batching hysteresis, producing kv probe floods -> kernel selection oscillation -> NIC TX queueing -> p99 spike on A10 L4 clusters. We'll log the tracer events and add an eval to catch this pattern. :thumbsup:
CI Bot: job 8822 (perf/latency-tests) now passed after rollback.
